1: import { Dependable, IConstruct, IDependable } from 'constructs';
2: import { PolicyStatement } from './policy-statement';
3: import { IGrantable, IPrincipal } from './principals';
4: import * as cdk from '../../core';
5: 
6: /**
7:  * Basic options for a grant operation
8:  *
9:  */
10: export interface CommonGrantOptions {
11:   /**
12:    * The principal to grant to
13:    *
14:    * @default if principal is undefined, no work is done.
15:    */
16:   readonly grantee: IGrantable;
17: 
18:   /**
19:    * The actions to grant
20:    */
21:   readonly actions: string[];
22: 
23:   /**
24:    * The resource ARNs to grant to
25:    */
26:   readonly resourceArns: string[];
27: 
28:   /**
29:    * Any conditions to attach to the grant
30:    *
31:    * @default - No conditions
32:    */
33:   readonly conditions?: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>;
34: }
35: 
36: /**
37:  * Options for a grant operation
38:  *
39:  */
40: export interface GrantWithResourceOptions extends CommonGrantOptions {
41:   /**
42:    * The resource with a resource policy
43:    *
44:    * The statement will be added to the resource policy if it couldn't be
45:    * added to the principal policy.
46:    */
47:   readonly resource: IResourceWithPolicy;
48: 
49:   /**
50:    * When referring to the resource in a resource policy, use this as ARN.
51:    *
52:    * (Depending on the resource type, this needs to be '*' in a resource policy).
53:    *
54:    * @default Same as regular resource ARNs
55:    */
56:   readonly resourceSelfArns?: string[];
57: }
58: 
59: /**
60:  * Options for a grant operation that only applies to principals
61:  *
62:  */
63: export interface GrantOnPrincipalOptions extends CommonGrantOptions {
64:   /**
65:    * Construct to report warnings on in case grant could not be registered
66:    *
67:    * @default - the construct in which this construct is defined
68:    */
69:   readonly scope?: IConstruct;
70: }
71: 
72: /**
73:  * Options for a grant operation to both identity and resource
74:  *
75:  */
76: export interface GrantOnPrincipalAndResourceOptions extends CommonGrantOptions {
77:   /**
78:    * The resource with a resource policy
79:    *
80:    * The statement will always be added to the resource policy.
81:    */
82:   readonly resource: IResourceWithPolicy;
83: 
84:   /**
85:    * When referring to the resource in a resource policy, use this as ARN.
86:    *
87:    * (Depending on the resource type, this needs to be '*' in a resource policy).
88:    *
89:    * @default Same as regular resource ARNs
90:    */
91:   readonly resourceSelfArns?: string[];
92: 
93:   /**
94:    * The principal to use in the statement for the resource policy.
95:    *
96:    * @default - the principal of the grantee will be used
97:    */
98:   readonly resourcePolicyPrincipal?: IPrincipal;
99: }
100: 
101: /**
102:  * Result of a grant() operation
103:  *
104:  * This class is not instantiable by consumers on purpose, so that they will be
105:  * required to call the Grant factory functions.
106:  */
107: export class Grant implements IDependable {
108:   /**
109:    * Grant the given permissions to the principal
110:    *
111:    * The permissions will be added to the principal policy primarily, falling
112:    * back to the resource policy if necessary. The permissions must be granted
113:    * somewhere.
114:    *
115:    * - Trying to grant permissions to a principal that does not admit adding to
116:    *   the principal policy while not providing a resource with a resource policy
117:    *   is an error.
118:    * - Trying to grant permissions to an absent principal (possible in the
119:    *   case of imported resources) leads to a warning being added to the
120:    *   resource construct.
121:    */
122:   public static addToPrincipalOrResource(options: GrantWithResourceOptions): Grant {
123:     const result = Grant.addToPrincipal({
124:       ...options,
125:       scope: options.resource,
126:     });
127: 
128:     const resourceAndPrincipalAccountComparison = options.grantee.grantPrincipal.principalAccount
129:       ? cdk.Token.compareStrings(options.resource.env.account, options.grantee.grantPrincipal.principalAccount)
130:       : undefined;
131:     // if both accounts are tokens, we assume here they are the same
132:     const equalOrBothUnresolved = resourceAndPrincipalAccountComparison === cdk.TokenComparison.SAME
133:       || resourceAndPrincipalAccountComparison == cdk.TokenComparison.BOTH_UNRESOLVED;
134:     const sameAccount: boolean = resourceAndPrincipalAccountComparison
135:       ? equalOrBothUnresolved
136:       // if the principal doesn't have an account (for example, a service principal),
137:       // we should modify the resource's trust policy
138:       : false;
139:     // If we added to the principal AND we're in the same account, then we're done.
140:     // If not, it's a different account and we must also add a trust policy on the resource.
141:     if (result.success && sameAccount) {
142:       return result;
143:     }
144: 
145:     const statement = new PolicyStatement({
146:       actions: options.actions,
147:       resources: (options.resourceSelfArns || options.resourceArns),
148:       principals: [options.grantee!.grantPrincipal],
149:     });
150: 
151:     const resourceResult = options.resource.addToResourcePolicy(statement);
152: 
153:     return new Grant({
154:       resourceStatement: statement,
155:       options,
156:       policyDependable: resourceResult.statementAdded ? resourceResult.policyDependable ?? options.resource : undefined,
157:     });
158:   }
159: 
160:   /**
161:    * Try to grant the given permissions to the given principal
162:    *
163:    * Absence of a principal leads to a warning, but failing to add
164:    * the permissions to a present principal is not an error.
165:    */
166:   public static addToPrincipal(options: GrantOnPrincipalOptions): Grant {
167:     const statement = new PolicyStatement({
168:       actions: options.actions,
169:       resources: options.resourceArns,
170:       conditions: options.conditions,
171:     });
172: 
173:     const addedToPrincipal = options.grantee.grantPrincipal.addToPrincipalPolicy(statement);
174:     if (!addedToPrincipal.statementAdded) {
175:       return new Grant({ principalStatement: undefined, options });
176:     }
177: 
178:     if (!addedToPrincipal.policyDependable) {
179:       throw new Error('Contract violation: when Principal returns statementAdded=true, it should return a dependable');
180:     }
181: 
182:     return new Grant({ principalStatement: statement, options, policyDependable: addedToPrincipal.policyDependable });
183:   }
184: 
185:   /**
186:    * Add a grant both on the principal and on the resource
187:    *
188:    * As long as any principal is given, granting on the principal may fail (in
189:    * case of a non-identity principal), but granting on the resource will
190:    * never fail.
191:    *
192:    * Statement will be the resource statement.
193:    */
194:   public static addToPrincipalAndResource(options: GrantOnPrincipalAndResourceOptions): Grant {
195:     const result = Grant.addToPrincipal({
196:       ...options,
197:       scope: options.resource,
198:     });
199: 
200:     const statement = new PolicyStatement({
201:       actions: options.actions,
202:       resources: (options.resourceSelfArns || options.resourceArns),
203:       principals: [options.resourcePolicyPrincipal || options.grantee!.grantPrincipal],
204:     });
205: 
206:     const resourceResult = options.resource.addToResourcePolicy(statement);
207:     const resourceDependable = resourceResult.statementAdded ? resourceResult.policyDependable ?? options.resource : undefined;
208: 
209:     return new Grant({
210:       principalStatement: statement,
211:       resourceStatement: result.resourceStatement,
212:       options,
213:       policyDependable: resourceDependable ? new CompositeDependable(result, resourceDependable) : result,
214:     });
215:   }
216: 
217:   /**
218:    * Returns a "no-op" `Grant` object which represents a "dropped grant".
219:    *
220:    * This can be used for e.g. imported resources where you may not be able to modify
221:    * the resource's policy or some underlying policy which you don't know about.
222:    *
223:    * @param grantee The intended grantee
224:    * @param _intent The user's intent (will be ignored at the moment)
225:    */
226:   public static drop(grantee: IGrantable, _intent: string): Grant {
227:     return new Grant({
228:       options: { grantee, actions: [], resourceArns: [] },
229:     });
230:   }
231: 
232:   /**
233:    * The statement that was added to the principal's policy
234:    *
235:    * @deprecated Use `principalStatements` instead
236:    */
237:   public readonly principalStatement?: PolicyStatement;
238: 
239:   /**
240:    * The statements that were added to the principal's policy
241:    */
242:   public readonly principalStatements = new Array<PolicyStatement>();
243: 
244:   /**
245:    * The statement that was added to the resource policy
246:    *
247:    * @deprecated Use `resourceStatements` instead
248:    */
249:   public readonly resourceStatement?: PolicyStatement;
250: 
251:   /**
252:    * The statements that were added to the principal's policy
253:    */
254:   public readonly resourceStatements = new Array<PolicyStatement>();
255: 
256:   /**
257:    * The options originally used to set this result
258:    *
259:    * Private member doubles as a way to make it impossible for an object literal to
260:    * be structurally the same as this class.
